name: Microsoft Intune
summary: Microsoft Intune manages Android, iOS and iPadOS, macOS, Windows, ChromeOS and Linux devices from one admin center. Plan 1 costs $8.00 per user a month on its own, and extras such as Remote Help and Endpoint Privilege Management are separate add-ons that need Plan 1. Devices register in Microsoft Entra ID before they enroll.

facts.text: Intune supports enrollment of Android, Android Enterprise, iOS, iPadOS, Linux, macOS and Windows devices, and a device must be registered in Microsoft Entra ID before it can enroll.
A tenant can submit up to 500 Wipe actions per day, counted across single-device actions, bulk actions and Graph API requests.
Remote lock only works well when a passcode or PIN is already set. Without one, the screen may turn off and the user can still use the device.
Remote lock is documented for Android Enterprise corporate-owned modes, AOSP, iOS and iPadOS, macOS and visionOS 2.0 or later. Windows is not on the list.

A compliance policy can lock a device remotely after it stays noncompliant for a set time. Blocking access to company resources needs Microsoft Entra Conditional Access, which in turn needs Entra ID P1 or P2.
Devices with no compliance policy assigned are marked Compliant by default, and an admin has to switch that setting to Not compliant to change it.

hiddenCosts: Most add-ons need an Intune Plan 1 subscription underneath them, so the real per-user price is the add-on plus $8.00.
The pricing page says prices may vary based on your Microsoft agreement and points to Contact Sales for a custom quote.
Windows Autopilot and Conditional Access enrollment steps need a Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 license.

contract.cancellation: Add-ons are sold as annual subscriptions that auto-renew. The pricing page states no cancellation terms for Plan 1 or the Suite.
